# Swete → Maranatha versification mapping source audit

AUDIT ONLY. No importer or application changes.

In-canon raw verse containers plus separate Baruch/Daniel components; out-of-canon files excluded. Witness alternatives run separately, never combined. Empty containers and numbered titles are counted as source records; detached body text is not assigned invented verse numbers.

Explicit reference clauses only form alignment hypotheses. Vendor-default mode separately traces numeric identity to SIL code; neither mode certifies WEB-C equivalence. Duplicate/conflicting clauses are retained, whereas the vendor runtime can overwrite or short-circuit them; this audit is not an emulation of that runtime. No count matching chooses or validates a mapping. STEP tests are retained as unevaluated conditions, all alternatives disclosed. Book namespaces ESG/EST and DAG/DAN are diagnostic bindings only; absence of a WEB-C-specific bridge remains a blocker.

The actual Paratext-related files are named org.vrs.txt (Original, Version=1.200), lxx.vrs.txt (Septuagint, Version=1.6), eng.vrs.txt (English, Version=2.0), vul.vrs.txt. No original.vrs or septuagint.vrs file was found under those long names in the inspected SIL resource tree. The public SIL library supplies these named resources; this is not a claim to have retrieved a proprietary Paratext installation. Copenhagen standard-mappings README explicitly calls its files standard Paratext mappings.

## 3. Per-book coverage


### SWORD LXX versus Vulg actual registrations

```text
		systemVersificationMgr->registerVersificationSystem("LXX", otbooks_lxx, ntbooks, vm_lxx);
		systemVersificationMgr->registerVersificationSystem("Vulg", otbooks_vulg, ntbooks_vulg, vm_vulg, mappings_vulg);
```

LXX registers verse limits without a mapping array; Vulg registers mappings_vulg. Vulg includes 273 encoded rule rows, including separate-book routing for EpJer/PrAzar/Sus/Bel. Those describe Vulg↔KJVA behavior, not an LXX→Vulg bridge. The missing LXX edge prevents applying them to Swete without guessing; zero evaluated edges below means unavailable, not no counterpart. The Vulg header explicitly describes a compromise across editions, not Nova Vulgata or WEB-C.

### Printed concordance — human check only

The fetched CCEL page reproduces a revised Brenton table and a separate list explicitly labeled “Swete p. 233”. Its columns distinguish Rahlfs/CATSS and Brenton, and the lower Swete list differs at several chapter divisions and subdivided clauses. It therefore reinforces the edition-specific blocker. No row from this printed-table transcription is expanded or used as machine correspondence by the script. Exact URL/date/hash is in the source inventory.

Kingdoms aliases are explicitly described in SIL lxx.vrs comments: 1SA/2SA = Orthodox 1/2 Kings, 1KI/2KI = Orthodox 3/4 Kings. Combined Esdras B corresponds to EZR in that file; EZR 11-23 → NEH is supplied by cited clauses, not an assumed -10 offset. Psalm superscriptions must retain 0, numbered title, and detached title distinctions. PRO has limits but no explicit rearrangement clauses in SIL/CA; native 29 chapters cannot be assumed aligned to a 31-chapter target. Daniel/Baruch components require explicit routes; namespaces alone cannot prove them. Esther prologue has no automatically invented numbered placement.

origVerse; GetVers(standardVerse) ?? standardVerse; numerical scheme default, NOT verified WEB-C equivalence"},{"url":"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Copenhagen-Alliance/versification-specification/5f3f82f3dc3cfd25fffc6ff04f3630763972258c/versification-mappings/standard-mappings/eng.json","pointer":"/mappedVerses/ESG 8:13","raw":"ESG 8:13 = ESG 8:12a"}],"intermediate":"ESG 8:12a"}],"reason":"candidate prediction only; WEB-C target namespace binding unverified","sourceDeclaredExcluded":false},"STEP-Greek":{"edges":[],"reason":"conditional STEP instructions only; STEP book identifiers use DAN/EST, not Paratext DAG/ESG; no verse renumbering or condition selection"},"STEP-alternatives":{"edges":[],"reason":"conditional STEP instructions only; STEP book identifiers use DAN/EST, not Paratext DAG/ESG; no verse renumbering or condition selection"},"SWORD-LXX/Vulg":{"edges":[],"reason":"No LXX mapping edge exists; Vulg table cannot supply it"},"BibleVersificationSystems":{"edges":[],"reason":"Repository contains README/LICENSE only, no tables"}} | {"EST 8:13":"The following is a copy of the letter containing orders: [The great King Ahasuerus sends greetings to the rulers of provinces in one hundred twenty-seven local governance regions, from India to Ethiopia, even to those who are faithful to our interests. Many who have been frequently honored by the most abundant kindness of theirbenefactors have conceived ambitious designs, and not only endeavor to hurt our subjects, but moreover, not being able to bear prosperity, they also endeavor to plot against their own benefactors. They not only would utterly abolish gratitude from among men, but also, elated by the boastings of men who are strangers to all that is good, they supposed that they would escape the sin-hating vengeance of the ever-seeing God. And oftentimes evil exhortation has made partakers of the guilt of shedding innocent blood, and has involved in irremediable calamities many of those who had been appointed to offices of authority, who had been entrusted with the management of their friends’ affairs; while men, by the false sophistry of an evil disposition, have deceived the simple goodwill of the ruling powers. And it is possible to see this, not so much from more ancient traditional accounts, as it is immediately in your power to see it by examining what things have been wickedly perpetrated by the baseness of men unworthily holding power. It is right to take heed with regard to the future, that we may maintain the government in undisturbed peace for all men, adopting needful changes, and ever judging those cases which come under our notice with truly equitable decisions. For whereas Haman, a Macedonian, the son of Hammedatha, in reality an alien from the blood of the Persians, and differing widely from our mild course of government, having been hospitably entertained by us, obtained so large a share of our universal kindness as to be called our father, and to continue the person next to the royal throne, reverenced of all; he however, overcome by pride, endeavored to deprive us of our dominion, and our life; having by various and subtle artifices demanded for destruction both Mordecai our deliverer and perpetual benefactor, and Esther the blameless consort of our kingdom, along with their whole nation. For by these methods he thought, having surprised us in a defenseless state, to transfer the dominion of the Persians to the Macedonians. But we find that the Jews, who have been consigned to destruction by the most abominable of men, are not malefactors, but living according to the most just laws, and being the sons of the living God, the most high and mighty, who maintains the kingdom, to us as well as to our forefathers, in the most excellent order. You will therefore do well in refusing to obey the letter sent by Haman the son of Hammedatha, because he who has done these things has been hanged with his whole family at the gates of Susa, Almighty God having swiftly returned to him a worthy punishment. We enjoin you then, having openly published a copy of this letter in every place, to give the Jews permission to use their own lawful customs and to strengthen them, that on the thirteenth of the twelfth month Adar, on the self-same day, they may defend themselves against those who attack them in a time of affliction. For in the place of the destruction of the chosen race, Almighty God has granted them this time of gladness. Therefore you also, among your notable feasts, must keep a distinct day with all festivity, that both now and hereafter it may be a day of deliverance to us and who are well disposed toward the Persians, but to those that plotted against us a memorial of destruction. And every city and province collectively, which shall not do accordingly, shall be consumed with vengeance by spear and fire. It shall be made not only inaccessible to men, but most hateful to wild beasts and birds forever.] Let the copies be posted in conspicuous places throughout the kingdom. Let all the Jews be ready against this day, to fight against their enemies."} |

| DAN 3:24 | They walked in the midst of the fire, praising God, and blessing the Lord. |
| DAN 3:25 | Then Azarias stood, and prayed like this. Opening his mouth in the midst of the fire he said, |
| DAN 3:49 | But the angel of the Lord came down into the furnace together with Azarias and his fellows, and he struck the flame of the fire out of the furnace, |
| DAN 3:50 | and made the midst of the furnace as it had been a moist whistling wind, so that the fire didn’t touch them at all. It neither hurt nor troubled them. |
| DAN 3:51 | Then the three, as out of one mouth, praised, glorified, and blessed God in the furnace, saying, |
| DAN 3:52 | “Blessed are you, O Lord, you God of our fathers, to be praised and exalted above all forever! |
| DAN 3:90 | O all you who worship the Lord, bless the God of gods, praise him, and give him thanks; for his mercy is forever!” Deliverance from the Furnace |
| DAN 3:91 | Then Nebuchadnezzar the king was astonished and rose up in haste. He spoke and said to his counselors, “Didn’t we cast three men bound into the middle of the fire?” They answered the king, “True, O king.” |
| DAN 3:97 | Then the king promoted Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego in the province of Babylon. |
| DAN 4:1 | Nebuchadnezzar the king, to all the peoples, nations, and languages, who dwell in all the earth: Peace be multiplied to you. |
| DAN 4:2 | It has seemed good to me to show the signs and wonders that the Most High God has worked toward me. |
| DAN 4:3 | How great are his signs! How mighty are his wonders! His kingdom is an everlasting kingdom. His dominion is from generation to generation. |
| DAN 13:1 | A man lived in Babylon, and his name was Joakim. |
| DAN 13:2 | He took a wife, whose name was Susanna, the daughter of Helkias, a very fair woman, and one who feared the Lord. |
| DAN 13:63 | Therefore Helkias and his wife praised God for their daughter Susanna, with Joakim her husband, and all the kindred, because there was no dishonesty found in her. |
| DAN 13:64 | And from that day forth, Daniel had a great reputation in the sight of the people. |
| DAN 14:1 | King Astyages was gathered to his fathers, and Cyrus the Persian received his kingdom. |
| DAN 14:2 | Daniel lived with the king, and was honored above all his friends. |
| DAN 14:41 | Then the king cried with a loud voice, saying, “Great are you, O Lord, you God of Daniel, and there is none other beside you!” |
| DAN 14:42 | So he drew him out, and cast those that were the cause of his destruction into the den; and they were devoured in a moment before his face. |

Observed boundary conclusion: WEB-C follows the Theodotion-associated arrangement at the inspected boundaries: 3:23 the bound men fall in, 3:24 walking/praising, 3:25 Azarias begins prayer; the three-voice hymn begins 3:51 with blessings at 3:52, deliverance resumes 3:91, and promotion occurs 3:97. Old Greek has a different 3:24 introductory sentence. Susanna closes with Daniel becoming great (WEB 13:64, Theodotion Sus 1:64); Old Greek instead ends with 62a/62b moralizing material. Bel begins with Astyages/Cyrus (WEB 14:1, Theodotion 1:1); Old Greek begins with a Habakkuk attribution. This is boundary evidence, not a statement about translation quality or every verse. Neither Swete witness is arranged as WEB-C chapters 13/14: components are separate. Both Swete Daniel chapter 3 witnesses retain 3:98-100 where WEB-C moves the royal proclamation to 4:1-3. The cached Theodotion Bel file stops mid-sentence at 1:36: WEB 14:41-42 cannot be checked against that source. Do not reconstruct it from Old Greek.

## Independent WEB-C target checks

| WEB-C ref | Actual target text |
| --- | --- |
| BAR 6:1 | A copy of a letter that Jeremy sent to those who were to be led captives into Babylon by the king of the Babylonians, to give them the message that God commanded him. |
| BAR 6:2 | Because of the sins which you have committed before God, you will be led away captives to Babylon by Nabuchodonosor king of the Babylonians. |
| BAR 6:50 | For seeing they are only wood and overlaid with gold and silver, it will be known hereafter that they are false. |
| BAR 6:51 | It will be manifest to all nations and kings that they are no gods, but the works of men’s hands, and that there is no work of God in them. |
| BAR 6:52 | Who then may not know that they are not gods? |
| BAR 6:72 | You will know them to be no gods by the bright purple that rots upon them. They themselves will be consumed afterwards, and will be a reproach in the country. |
| BAR 6:73 | Better therefore is the just man who has no idols; for he will be far from reproach. |

Letter of Jeremiah source verse 1 begins the captivity warning, whereas WEB BAR 6:1 is the prose letter introduction and BAR 6:2 begins the captivity warning. Generic eng.vrs predicts source 1 → BAR 6:1; STEP Greek also predicts BAR 6:1. These predictions fail this boundary check. At the end, generic eng.vrs predicts LJE 1:72 → BAR 6:72; STEP Greek predicts BAR 6:73. The actual closing maxim occurs in source verse 72 and WEB 6:73. These observations do NOT authorize a hand-written correction: no audited external full WEB-C bridge was found. The Swete prose introduction is detached body text and must not be assigned a source verse without a cited policy.

Psalms: generic eng.vrs targets numeric verse 0 for titles; canon has no 0 slot. LXX 9:22 has overlapping original-scheme clauses (10:0 and 10:1), retained as a conflict rather than silently overwritten. Exact predicted splits are printed above from external rows. Jeremiah 25:14 predictions differ among Greek traditions and source metadata; equal chapter totals are irrelevant. Esther expanded English ESG numbering is not WEB-C EST numbering: several predicted addition targets exceed actual canon limits. SIL and Copenhagen share ancestry, so their agreement is not independent evidence.

## 6. Proposed smallest static shape — DESIGN ONLY


```js
window.MARANATHA_LXX_MAPPING = {
  scheme: "<approved Swete-to-WEB-C scheme id>",
  sourceCommit: "<pinned Swete commit>",
  targetCanonSHA256: "<canon hash>",
  provenance: [/* { url, commit, sha256, license } */],
  entries: {
    "<Swete witness/book/chapter/verse>": {
      to: [/* canon references; [] ONLY for externally attested no counterpart */],
      p: [/* [provenanceIndex, external line or JSON pointer] per entry */]
    }
  }
};
```

An absent entry means unresolved, never identity or no counterpart. Retain separate witness IDs, segment suffixes, zero/title references and original text; to may have multiple destinations without splitting or rewriting text. This is a symbolic schema, not real mapping entries. Load through a script tag; no local fetch(). Runtime adapter would index cited source refs per canon cell while preserving text and source citation. Covered book with no mapped verse can use existing missing-verse state; absent source book uses missing-book. Unresolved mapping must carry a distinct explanation and remain outside aligned rows, rather than claiming textual absence. Existing separate versification display can carry native unresolved passages. Inspect VerseAvailability states before implementation; do not silently concatenate or duplicate Scripture when multiple sources feed one cell.

validate.mjs would need an optional mapping-aware path: validate source refs against the exact native witness corpus, destination refs against canon, provenance and licenses for every entry, explicit [] versus unknown, all multiplicities and collisions, exclusions and unmapped coverage, witness consistency, canon/source hashes, and semantic regression anchors. Source-native chapter/verse counts must not be compared directly to canon counts as alignment validation. Retain current validation for existing translations. Provisional canon entries are not permission to hide out-of-range mappings. All changes remain design only.

## RECOMMENDATION


No evaluated source is a complete verified Swete → current WEB-C canon mapping. Use licensed Copenhagen/Paratext data as a starting reference, not a ready importer table. SIL and Copenhagen are alternatives with shared ancestry; combining them is not independent corroboration. A future hybrid may be needed for edition-specific Swete references and WEB-C additions/title conventions, but every extra edge must come from a separately cited licensed source. STEP is a rich cross-check candidate with conditional Greek alternatives; its conflicting redistribution wording must be clarified before shipping data derived from it. SWORD Vulg cannot fill the missing SWORD LXX correspondence edge.

## BLOCKERS


- Establish a licensed, external WEB-C-specific bridge; generic English, Vulgate, Original and Greek schemes are not interchangeable.
- Resolve externally, not by local fixes: Letter introduction/offset, Esther addition references, native Proverbs ordering and superscriptions.
- Obtain independent passage-level evidence for Jeremiah order and the Greek tradition used by each Swete book; retain candidate disagreements.
- Decide Daniel witness and separate-component placement with cited edges; incomplete Theodotion Bel remains a raw-source gap.
- Clarify STEP redistribution grant and GPL restrictions before using either for app data.
- Preserve explicit unknown versus no counterpart and multiplicity; verify body titles/introductions without inventing source references.
- User approval is required before any importer, mapping dataset or application/validator changes. STOP after audit.
